title: The HWMCC 2019 and 2020 models as CNF, examples
why: The hardware competition moved from AIGER to BTOR2 in 2019, and nobody distributes those models as formulas. This pack is the bit-vector models of the two editions in CNF, at three depths, produced by one pinned chain: btor2aiger bit blasts, aigmove and aigunroll expand, and the plain Tseitin encoder of the aiger examples writes the formula — the same encoder the AIGER pack uses, so the two sit side by side.

items.note: two of the small models from each submitter and year of the bit-vector track, at three depths. The array track is out: btor2aiger cannot bit blast an unbounded array

permission: to ask: the models are distributed by the competition, the CNF is derived from them by a pinned chain
size_note: measured on rast-p00 of the 2020 edition: 5177 clauses at depth 5, 45305 at depth 10, 151145 at depth 20. The depth is what makes the formula grow, and the models differ by two orders of magnitude in state, so the pack keeps nothing past 300 thousand clauses and gives each instance five minutes.
floor_note: A depth under the model's reachability horizon gives nothing to solve: aigunroll's constant propagation proves the property unreachable while it unrolls, the encoder writes the two-clause formula, and every model that hits it writes the same file. Such a formula is left out, with the depth that produced it recorded, and so is a formula a name already in this pack produced.
example_note: a pack is a handful of small formulas, meant to be looked at, not a benchmark suite: the sizes a solver author needs are produced on demand with the same pinned chain, by raising the depth or picking another model

skip_reasons.3: btor2aiger could not bit blast the model, which is what an array model gets
skip_reasons.4: the encoder refused the unrolled circuit

regenerate: tools/fetch_upstream.py hwmcc20 && docker run --rm -v "$CACHE/hwmcc20/files/btor2/bv/<year>/<submitter>:/data:ro" satex-gen/btor2:2026 unroll <depth> <model>.btor

built.chain: btor2aiger bit blasts, aigmove and aigunroll expand over k time frames, then poormanaigtocnf writes the formula

coverage_note: 19 formulas from eight models at depths 5, 10 and 20, chosen two per submitter and year of the bit-vector track. Twenty combinations are left out, every one by a limit of ours: eleven under the clause floor, five past 300 thousand clauses and four past five minutes, which is what the real designs of these editions cost — ridecore, picorv32 and zipcpu are not toy circuits. The eleven under the floor are four models whose property no depth of this grid can reach: aigunroll proves it while unrolling and the encoder writes the two-clause formula, the same file every time, so the models leave the pack rather than fill it with one formula under eight names. The array track is not in the pack at all: btor2aiger cannot bit blast an unbounded array, and the bridge says so rather than guessing.
